voyage.name: Hafengeburtstag
voyage.content: Every year in May the harbour birthday attracts millions of people. Dozens of stands and stages, a ship parade, and changing events are organised to celebrate the cities spring of wealth. The harbour dates from 1189. Since then, the Harbour Birthday has grown into the greatest harbour party in the world. It is generally in early May.

voyage.name: Kirschblütenfest
voyage.content: On May 19, the Japanese community of Hamburg celebrates the Japanese Cherry Blossom Festival by the Lake Alster. Enormous fireworks and a peaceful atmosphere are characteristics of this event.

voyage.name: Hamburger Dom
voyage.content: The Dom is one of the largest fairs in Germany. The streets of the fairground, lined on both sides with rides, amusements and food and drink stalls, are some 3.3 km long. It takes place for three separate months in spring, summer, and early winter.

voyage.name: Hauptkirche St. Michaelis
voyage.content: The youngest and most famous of the five is also the only baroque church. This building is not the original St. Michaelis - that one (built 1647-1669) was destroyed by a lightning strike in 1750. It was not until 1786 that the present church was erected on the site. From the tower (450 steps, or take the elevator) you'll have a great view over the city. Entry to the church is free, but the tower and the crypt cost ex

voyage.name: Hauptkirche St. Jacobi
voyage.content: St. Jacobi has been a parish since the 12th century, when it was not even within Hamburg's then city walls. The present-day church is a reconstruction of the late medieval one from the 15th century, which was destroyed during the Second World War. The reconstruction afforded St. Jacobi with a visibly modern roof and steeple.

voyage.name: Hauptkirche St. Petri
voyage.content: St. Petri was a cathedral as early as the 12th century or possibly even earlier. As with other Hauptkirchen, the present version is one of many successive, and was only completed in 1878 after the great fire in 1842 consumed its predecessor. In turn, however, St. Petri survived the Second World War relatively intact. Of note are the large ornate door handles in the shape of lion heads, which have survived both the fi

voyage.name: Hauptkirche St. Nikolai
voyage.price: The price to take the elevator is €5 for adults and €4 for groups of at least 10 people
voyage.content: All five main churches of Hamburg were damaged in World War II. But in contrast to the other four, St. Nikolai has not been re-erected making it a memorial against war. It was designed by English architect George Gilbert Scott. The steeple is still standing and visitors can take an elevator to the top for a view of the city.

voyage.name: Hauptkirche St. Katharinen
voyage.content: Situated on an island, it traditionally served as the church of the seamen. The base of its spire, dating from the 13th century, is the second oldest building preserved in the city. The church is also famous for its centuries-old organ, played by Bach when he was visiting the city. The instrument was actually destroyed to a large extent by the wartime bombings, but has been meticulously rebuilt and is playable again.

voyage.name: Hulbe-Haus
voyage.content: Dating from the beginning of the 20th century as most buildings around, but looking much older.

voyage.name: Radio Hamburg
voyage.content: Under the building you can visit the remains of the bishops tower, from the 11th century. On the other side of the road, you can see excavations in progress, seeking the remains of the small fortress Hammaburg, which was erected in the 9th century giving Hamburg its name.

voyage.name: Rathaus
voyage.price: €7 for adults, €5,50 for Hamburg Card holders and free for children under 14
voyage.content: Hamburg's impressive city hall was built in 1897 out of sandstone in neo-Renaissance style, including a 112-m tower. The square in front of the city hall is the Rathausmarkt, hosting many events especially in summer. Inside there are several magnificent halls used for representative purposes and sittings of government and parliament. These can be visited in guided tours (M-Th 10:00-15:15, F-Su 10:00-13:15, half-hourl

voyage.name: Hamburger Börse
voyage.content: Between the buildings, there is a little courtyard called Rathaushof with its fountain, Hygieia-Brunnen.

voyage.name: Wall-Anlagen
voyage.content: The western part of the former city wall is nowadays a park area surrounding the inner city as a semicircle, ranging from the Landungsbrücken (Helgoländer Allee) up to Binnenalster. In the Wallanlagen there's a big playground and in the winter an ice rink. There also the impressive Hanseatic Courthouse building.

voyage.name: Patriotische Gesellschaft
voyage.content: The building of the Patriotic Society was erected following the great fire of 1842 on the former site of the old town hall of Hamburg. Built using the most modern technology at that time, including concrete substructure, and featuring modern techology such as flush toilets, it was nevertheless kept in a style that was an interpretation of the surrounding medieval architectural heritage. Of note inside is the large ha

voyage.name: Trostbrücke
voyage.content: It has statues of Graf Adolf III and Bishop Ansgar on both sides.

voyage.name: Zollenbrücke
voyage.content: Hamburg's oldest remaining bridge from the 17th century

voyage.name: Chilehaus
voyage.content: The house, depicting the form of a ship, is probably the best example of the 1920s style of "Kontorhaus" architecture. Large office buildings are displayed in the typical, northern red brick style.

voyage.name: Hopfenmarkt
voyage.content: The hop market with its fountain Vierländerinbrunnen

voyage.name: Alte Deichstraße
voyage.content: Ensemble of traditional half-timbered merchant houses.

voyage.name: Nicolai Fleet
voyage.content: This is the site where Hamburg's harbour was some centuries ago.

voyage.name: Kleiner Michel
voyage.content: Built after the reformation, it's functioned as a Catholic church since the 19th century.

voyage.name: The Hamburg Dungeon
voyage.content: A live-action presentation of the "darker times" of Hamburg. It is probably mostly suited for a younger, easily impressed audience. But it might not be suitable for young children.

voyage.name: The Miniatur Wunderland
voyage.price: Tickets €20, kids under 16 €12.50. Flexible ticket with VR €30
voyage.content: The world's largest model railway layout. The panoramas include parts of Hamburg, the Alps, the American west, South America, and a Scandinavian exhibit which features automated ships on a body of water. It also has an airport exhibit with automated planes which taxi and fly, even having simulated delays to mimic a real-world airport. Advance booking by at least two weeks strongly recommended due to high demand.

voyage.name: Viewpoint towards the water castle
voyage.content: One of the more famous photo spots in Hamburg on Poggenmühle bridge.

voyage.name: Kaffeemuseum Burg
voyage.content: At its heart this is a cafe serving good coffee set up to show aspects of the coffee trade however the point of going there is to see inside one of the famous warehouses of Speicherstadt. It is popular with tourists and deservedly so. The main timbers of the warehouse are massive and plainly built with a view to longevity.

voyage.name: Elbphilharmonie
voyage.content: New 'architectural lighthouse' of Hamburg. On the top of a huge old warehouse a 110 metres tall modern philharmonic hall with glass façade and wave-shaped roof. It also includes a fancy hotel, restaurant, as well as private apartments. Access to the observation deck (called "Plaza") is free (although you need to get a ticket to prevent overcrowding), and offers a great view of Hamburg. On days of long queues in front

voyage.name: HafenCity Kesselhaus InfoCenter
voyage.content: Here you can find information about the new buildings and the whole district. The InfoCenter also provides free guided tours.

voyage.name: HafenCity View Point
voyage.content: Look at the erecting process from an orange observation tower, which allows nice views on the HafenCity, the harbour, and the river.

voyage.name: City und Sportboothafen
voyage.content: Hamburg's city and yacht harbour.

voyage.name: Feuerschiff LV 13
voyage.content: The big red lighthouse ship hosts a restaurant today.

voyage.name: Überseebrücke
voyage.content: This is where big cruise liners used to dock when coming to Hamburg.

voyage.name: Gruner + Jahr
voyage.content: Hyper-modern building of the publishers.

voyage.name: Krameramtswohnungen
voyage.content: The shopkeeper-office-flats are the last example of a typical 17th-century housing estate.

voyage.name: Flussschifferkirche
voyage.content: Germany's only floating church in Rothenburgsort.

voyage.name: Tropengewächshaus
voyage.hours: Mar–Oct: Mon-Fri 09:00–16:45; Sat Sun and bank holidays 10:00–17:45; Nov–Feb: Mon-Fri 09:00–15:45; Sat Sun 10:00–17:45

voyage.name: Portugiesenviertel
voyage.content: Especially during the warmer months the area around Ditmar-Koel-Straße has a very special flair. Lots of restaurants and shops invite one to linger.

voyage.name: Kunsthalle
voyage.price: Adults €14, concessions €8, family day ticket €18, under 18 free admission
voyage.content: Glockengießerwall north of Hauptbahnhof. The museum houses an important collection of paintings from the 19th century with works from Max Liebermann, Lovis Corinth, Philipp Otto Runge, Caspar David Friedrich, Adolf Menzel, and modern arts. It rises on both sides of a paved court. The Baroque building on one side has the older works. The areas under the courtyard and the other, modern looking building house an extensi

voyage.name: Deichtorhallen
voyage.content: The Deichtorhallen is one of the best known exhibition galleries worldwide. The historical buildings are divided into an exhibition hall for contemporary art and the "House of Photography". Together the two buildings organize a highly diverse program of changing exhibitions.

voyage.name: Hamburg Museum
voyage.content: Holstenwall, close to Underground station "St. Pauli". This is the museum of city history, bringing the past to life with a lot of models showing the development of the harbour and the city. The club "MEHEV" is showing a 40-year-old and one of the largest scale model railroads here.

voyage.name: Internationales Maritimes Museum
voyage.content: This private museum in near the Speicherstadt district houses Peter Tamm's collection of model ships, construction plans, uniforms, and maritime art,. It opened in 2008 in the refurbished Kaispeicher B (quay warehouse B), which is the oldest preserved warehouse in Hamburg, having been built in 1879. Covering ten floors it is one of the most comprehensive maritime museums in the world with 1,000 large and 36,000 minia

voyage.name: Speicherstadtmuseum
voyage.content: Branch of Museum of Labour in docklands warehouse. History of the district and tea and coffee trade.

voyage.name: Cap San Diego
voyage.content: One of the last generation of pre-containerisation cargo ships (built in the 1960s), now semi-permanently moored halfway between Landungsbrücken and the Speicherstadt, and is the largest functional cargo museum ship in the world. The ship has been restored and is maintained in full working order by volunteers (who take it out a few times a year, notably during the Hafengeburtstag celebration). You can visit the ship

voyage.name: Automuseum Prototyp
voyage.content: Museum of car prototypes, nice shop inside.

voyage.name: Spicey's Gewürzmuseum
voyage.content: Located in the Speicherstadt. They claim to be the world's only spice museum.

voyage.name: Chocoversum Hachez Schokoladen-Museum
voyage.price: €14, discounts for children, disabled, families and large groups
voyage.content: The Chocoversum is a "museum" run by chocolate manufacturer Hachez from Hamburg's fellow Hansestadt Bremen. Rather than focus on exhibiting historic artifacts, it presents the process of making chocolate from the plantation up to the finished confection. There is also a studio where visitors can try their hands at being a chocolatier. 90-minute guided tours are provided everyday.

voyage.name: Rickmer Rickmers
voyage.content: A museum sailing ship (three-masted bark) from 1896, permanently moored off the Landungsbrücken. On board is a museum, a small restaurant, and an escape room.

voyage.name: Dialog im Dunkeln
voyage.content: Sighted people get to experience the everyday life of blind people. In completely dark rooms blind people guide the sighted through the exhibition.

voyage.name: Hamburgische Staatsoper
voyage.content: Hamburg is home to the Hamburg State Opera House, one of the leading opera houses in Germany. It holds great historical significance, as in 1678 the first public opera house in Germany was built in Hamburg at Gänsemarkt Square, which is where the opera house is still today.

voyage.name: Laeiszhalle
voyage.content: The Laeiszhalle is the main classical music hall in Hamburg, with two halls: the kleiner Saal and großer Saal. You can see the schedule on their website. For online ticket purchases, use Ticket Online.

voyage.name: The Rover Rep Theatre
voyage.content: At the Irish Rover. English language pub theatre under the Irish Rover at the Großneumarkt. High class professional productions in a special atmosphere.

voyage.name: Thalia Theater
voyage.content: New directors and the continuing cooperation with young important writers based on the confidence in a strong and vital company lead to international acknowledgment.

voyage.name: Alsterarkaden
voyage.content: The white arcades over the canal are Hamburg's prime shopping location

voyage.name: Europa Passage
voyage.content: The most frequented shopping complex in downtown Hamburg, near the town hall at the Alster lake.

voyage.name: Hanse Viertel
voyage.content: A large shopping centre, erected in early 20th century

voyage.name: Alsterhaus
voyage.content: One of the oldest department stores in Hamburg.

voyage.name: Spitaler Straße / Mönckebergstraße
voyage.content: The area west of Hamburg's central railway station is mainly a shopping district.

voyage.name: Souvenirs
voyage.content: A good and not-overpriced souvenir shop is on the town hall square under the glass roofage. Typical souvenirs are statues of the Michel Church or the town hall, the water-carrying dogsbody Hummel hummel Mors mors, blue road signs like Reeperbahn, and a post card of the red light district.

voyage.name: Kartoffelkeller
voyage.content: Large range of dishes with potatoes at their heart, including lots of traditional German dishes, e.g. Herring and Potatoes.

voyage.name: Cafe Paris
voyage.content: Classic French bistro in a beautiful historical building. Good place to get a coffee and pastry, or enjoy a leisurely lunch. Ground floor is very loud, crowded and busy. Upstairs (when entering turn right) is a quiet restaurant with a small bar (all food is also served at the bar). "Tartar" and "steak frites" can be strongly recommended.

voyage.name: Vapiano
voyage.content: A chain, Vapiano serves Italian food, in a trendy, friendly atmosphere. By the entrance you will get a "credit card", you show when you order food in the different kitchens. You pay when you leave.

voyage.name: Fleetschlösschen
voyage.content: Fish dishes, frikadellen and labskaus on the menu, in other words local cuisine.

voyage.name: Old Commercial Room
voyage.content: Founded in 1795, this upscale restaurant is best known for fish dishes and labskaus (Northern German variant of hash).

voyage.name: Mama Mia
voyage.content: Cozy Italian restaurant known for its welcoming atmosphere, friendly service, and authentic homemade pasta.

voyage.name: Brauhaus Joh. Albrecht
voyage.content: Cosy brewpub with good beers and food.

voyage.name: Chaplin's Pub
voyage.content: Cosy dive pub near the station - cash only.

voyage.name: Jugendherberge Hamburg - Auf dem Stintfang
voyage.content: Priceless river/harbour view and in walking distance to the Reeperbahn.

voyage.name: Barceló Hamburg
voyage.content: Thoroughly modern business hotel in the second row of buildings to Binnenalster, which is visible over the rooftops of neighbouring buildings from the hotel's top floor. All the facilities you may expect, but the gym is an extremely small and narrow room.

voyage.name: AMERON Hotel Speicherstadt
voyage.content: A comfortable, modern hotel with interesting interior appointments right within Speicherstadt

voyage.name: Lindner Hotel Am Michel
voyage.content: Lindner is a chain of German upscale'ish hotels with nothing particularly special, but solid service standards and well-appointed rooms. The hotel's name is a bit of a stretch, as it is not immediately next to St. Michaelis church.

voyage.name: Scandic Hamburg Emporio
voyage.content: One of the Swedish chain's southernmost outposts is an all-new hotel opened in 2014, with an architecturally interesting building and Scandinavian flair throughout, meaning minimalist but tasteful appointments and lots of wood. Relatively large rooms, but most with views of opposite walls. Location on the edge of Neustadt is quite convenient for those visiting the CCH.

voyage.name: JUFA Hotel Hamburg HafenCity
voyage.content: Child-friendly hotel with family rooms of different sizes and playgrounds both indoors and outdoors.

voyage.name: Hotel Baseler Hof
voyage.price: sgl from €89, dbl from €145, both incl. breakfast
voyage.content: Opened in 1907, the hotel was remodeled in 2000 to its current form. Wi-Fi is available. The hotels has many conference rooms for up to 200 persons, a sauna and a fitness studio. There's also a restaurant; Kaffee- und Weinhaus Kleinhuis.

voyage.name: Fairmont Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten
voyage.content: Complementing the Atlantic on the other side of the Kennedybruecke as one of Hamburg's finest and oldest hotels, Vier Jahreszeiten has been overlooking the Binnenalster since the early 20th century, expanded and refurbished many times since. Today it is managed by Fairmont Hotels and Resorts and provides most comforts and amenities a contemporary luxury hotel can, but be aware that it has no swimming pool and the fit

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Hamburg
voyage.content: The Hyatt took residence in an exquisitely-decorated historic building, and provides an oasis of relaxed tranquility in the busy area neighbouring the Hauptbahnhof. Rising to the challenge of fellow luxury hotels in Hamburg, the Park Hyatt offers no less than 1000 sqm of spa and fitness facilities.

voyage.name: Marriott
voyage.content: 4-Star hotel with 270 guest rooms and 8 suites, also has a Body Care Centre with indoor pool and whirlpool as well as 416 m² conference facilities. Restaurant and piano bar with live music.

voyage.name: SIDE
voyage.content: Under the unassuming name you will find one of Hamburg's finest design hotels, rivaled perhaps only by the Sofitel. Rooms are kept in minimalist white and are protected from any outside interference by a double facade. The SkyLounge on the 8th floor features a unique view of the city.

voyage.name: Sofitel Hamburg Alter Wall
voyage.content: Quite nondescript on the outside, the Sofitel shines inside with perfectly balanced and tasteful minimalist design, and of course great service standards.

voyage.name: Steigenberger Hotel Hamburg
voyage.content: Situated right on the Alsterfleet, the Steigenberger is housed in a building made to look in line with Hamburg's traditional canal architecture. Inside you will find the usual German idea of Gemuetlichkeit combined with the chain's usual high standards of service. Of note is the gym and spa area with views over the neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Renaissance Hamburg Hotel
voyage.content: The Renaissance is located in an interesting early 20th century building, which is a part of the Hanseviertel. Inside a bit dated, but with the usual Marriott quality.

voyage.name: Altonaer Museum
voyage.content: Dedicated to Altona's, Hamburg's and northern Germany's cultural history.

voyage.name: Altona City Hall
voyage.content: Built in 1898, when Altona was still a separate city. It's an impressive building with influences of Italian Renaissance.

voyage.name: Dockland
voyage.content: Walk 136 steps to the roof of this building to get a wonderful view of the harbour. The six-storey glass and steel building has the shape of a parallelogram and is reminiscent of a ship bow.

voyage.name: Altonaer Volkspark
voyage.content: This used to be the city park of the independent town of Altona. Unlike Hamburger Stadtpark, this park has been left in a more natural state. On the northern edge of the park is Volksparkstadion, the home stadium of the football team HSV, as well as the multi-purpose Barclaycard Arena.

voyage.name: Landungsbrücken
voyage.content: The most touristy part of Hamburg's harbour, close to the metro station with the same name. Piers connected with several bridges swim on the water adapting to the tide. There tourist boats land and you will find souvenir shops, restaurants, and snack bars. The sailing ship Rickmer Rickmers can be visited. The old passenger docks, from which (among many others) many of the emigrants to the Americas from eastern Europe

voyage.name: U-434
voyage.content: One of the biggest non-nuclear Soviet submarines, moored near to the Fischmarkt. Guided tours are possible.

voyage.name: Alter Elbtunnel
voyage.content: Completed in 1911, it links both sides of the river Elbe. A lift or stairs bring you the 24 m down into the tunnel. You then walk through one of its two 427-m-long pipes having 12 m of water over your head. At the other side, you again walk up the stairs or take a lift. The tunnel is decorated with ceramic arts of maritime motifs (e.g. fish, mussels, seals, old boots). For pedestrians and bicycles it is free and open

voyage.name: Museumshafen Oevelgönne
voyage.content: Historical boats.

voyage.name: Hamburger Dom
voyage.hours: Three times a year (Mar, Aug, and Nov)
voyage.content: A large fair held at Heiligengeistfeld fair ground. With three fairs (spring, summer and winter) per year it is the biggest and the longest fair throughout Germany and attracts every one approximately ten million visitors per year.

voyage.name: Reeperbahn
voyage.content: A street and entertainment district in Hamburg's St. Pauli district, one of the two centres of Hamburg's nightlife (with Schanze) and also the city's major red-light district. In German it is also called die sündigste Meile (the most sinful mile) and nicknamed Kiez. The Reeperbahn Festival is among the largest club festivals.

voyage.name: Panoptikum
voyage.content: A wax cabinet with a history of over 125 years and as such the oldest in Germany, though it has been in its current location since the 1950s. Not as big and famous as Madame Tussauds in London, nevertheless the figures have been created with love for details. Some of the older figures aren't as detailed, though that's because there were less tools and knowledge about working with wax figures back then.

voyage.name: Flakturm IV
voyage.content: Right at the Heiligengeistfeld is a World War II bunker, visible from far away due to its size. Nowadays the building houses different media companies and agentures, and there's a dance club on the upper floor.

voyage.name: St. Pauli Archiv
voyage.content: Archive for the city district and history workshop. Arranges very interesting themed walks around St. Pauli.

voyage.name: Hafenstraße
voyage.content: The street was a place for squatters in the 1980s and was well known by the media when there were "battles" between the Autonomous movement and the police. Some squats still exist there, though the "80s-Myth" is dead. You can go to the Punksbar "onkel otto" or eat at the "VoKü" ("Volxküche" - a group cooking event, at which the meal is served free of charge or at cost).

voyage.name: Beatles-Platz
voyage.content: There is a sculpture honouring the Beatles. Also in the Reeperbahn area are clubs where the Beatles played at various times from 1960 to 1962, including the Indra club and Star Club.

voyage.name: Grosse Freiheit
voyage.content: In the pedestrian street there are a lot of bars and clubs - a great place to go in the evening, although it's very crowded and it may get a bit dangerous in the weekend. On weekdays, it is harmless here - a low-budget tip is, 99 Cent Bar, which offers really many drinks for basically €1. On the weekend, you will have to pay an entrance fee of €1 but it's still the best place to go drinking on a budget. The street wa

voyage.name: Hans-Albers-Platz
voyage.content: Between Reeperbahn and Herbertstraße there's a memorial for an actor who was advertising the Kiez (Reeperbahn). Especially the movie Große Freiheit Nummer 7 helped making the Kiez famous.

voyage.name: Herbertstraße
voyage.content: The epicenter of the red-light district, this short street runs parallel to Reeperbahn is closed off by gates from both ends. Adults only and photography is strictly banned.

voyage.name: Spielbudenplatz
voyage.content: The place got its name from the entertainers putting up shows here for sailors from all over the world back in the day. For example Mr. Hagenback (who opened the zoo park in the city) showcased his sea lions here. Today it is surrounded by several venues including St. Pauli theater, Schmidt's Tivoli , Schmidt's Theater and Operettenhaus.

voyage.name: Rote Flora
voyage.content: This building used to be the last squatted house in Hamburg, it's now left to the squatters for free by the owner. During the week, it is turned into a café, concerts of various styles or other events may also take place. On some days there is cheap (mostly vegan) food available. You can sometimes find fantastic parties for small prices on Friday and Saturday.

voyage.name: Christianskirche
voyage.content: Baroque church in Ottensen.

voyage.name: Zeise Hallen
voyage.content: The halls were built in 1857 for the Zeise company manufacturing ship parts. The company went bust in 1979, and nowadays the cultural heritage building is used as a cultural center with a movie theater.

voyage.name: Planten un Blomen
voyage.hours: Daily open until 23:00, in April until 22:00. Greenhouses are open during the summer season (Mar-Oct): Mon-Fri 09:00-16:45, Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-17:45, winter season (Nov-Feb) Mon-Fri 09:00-15:45, Sat Sun, holidays 10:00-15:45
voyage.content: This park is partially on the old city wall of Hamburg. Already in the 1930s the former zoological park was remodeled into a bird and entertainment park for the Lower German Garden Exhibition (Niederdeutsche Gartenschau). Afterwards it was rebuilt for three international garden shows in 1953, 1963 and 1973. The botanical garden was turned into a park landscape, and was moved to Klein Flottbek in Altona in 1979. The t

voyage.name: Jenisch park
voyage.content: The oldest landscaped park in Hamburg. Two museums, Jenisch House and Ernst Barlach House, are in the park. Flottbek River flows through the park and into the Elbe at Teufelsbrück.

voyage.name: Baurs Park
voyage.content: Nice park with views to the Elbe river.

voyage.name: Loki Schmidt Garten
voyage.hours: Daily open from 09:00 to about 1 hour before sunset
voyage.content: For a century and a half, the botanical garden was situated in the current Planten un Blomen park, where the tropical greenhouses still remain. In 1979, the botanical garden was relocated to its current place in the Klein Flottbek district. In the southern part of the park there are several themed gardens with medical plants, farm plants, plants featured in the Bible, conifers, fragnant plants, poisonous plants, thre

voyage.name: St. Pauli Theater
voyage.content: It opened in 1841 as the Urania Theater and took its present name in 1941.

voyage.name: Schmidt Theater
voyage.content: Schmidt Theater is a private theater at Spielbudenplatz. It consists of two venues, the Schmidt Theater itself and the Schmidts Tivoli (also known as Grosses Haus), which is just a stone's throw away.

voyage.name: Schmidt-Theater
voyage.content: Theatre, variety, cabaret, concerts, and satirical revues.

voyage.name: Schmidts Tivoli
voyage.content: Avant-garde shows and high-class musicals. The world-famous musical Cabaret and the successful musical compendium Fifty Fifty were staged here.

voyage.name: Pulverfass
voyage.content: Travestieshow

voyage.name: Hafenrundfahrten
voyage.content: From Landungsbrücken, you can make boat tours into the harbour, available from various companies and take around an hour. Big ships provide more comfort, but smaller ships also go through the Speicherstadt. Both are well worth the money. Inquire about English language tours.

voyage.name: HADAG Ferries
voyage.content: A low-budget alternative for a boat tour on the river Elbe. A part of Hamburg's public transport system (HVV). If you have already bought a HVV day ticket, the ride is free. Most tourists take ferry 62 from Landungsbrücken to Finkenwerder, via Neumühlen with the museum harbour Oevelgönne. The whole ride to Finkenwerder and return takes about an hour, and on weekends with good weather this ferry will be very full. In

voyage.name: On Stage
voyage.content: Fitness center and dance studio.

voyage.name: Hamburger SV
voyage.content: Die Rothosen (The Red Shorts) were promoted in 2025 and play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. Volksparkstadion has a capacity of 57,000 for domestic games and 51,500 for internationals and occasionally hosts concerts. In 2024 it hosted matches in the UEFA Euro Finals.

voyage.name: FC St Pauli
voyage.content: The Kiezkicker ("Neighbourhood Kickers") were relegated in 2026 and now play soccer in 2. Bundesliga, the second tier. Millerntor-Stadion has a capacity of 29,500 and is also used for concerts.

voyage.name: Hot Dogs
voyage.content: Best assorted true vintage and deadstock clothing of the past 15 to 90 years you will be able to find at Hot Dogs.

voyage.name: Kleidermarkt
voyage.content: New and second-hand.

voyage.name: St. Pauli Fischmarkt
voyage.content: For Germans, it's a classic to eat bread with fish on St. Pauli Fischmarkt, especially very early in the Sunday morning (meaning 05:00 - 09:30) when visiting Hamburg. If for breakfast or as an after-party snack may depend on your inner clock, but if you are a fresh fish lover it is absolutely worth it since this fish was just fished during the night in Nordsee.

voyage.name: Joker
voyage.content: Great for a quick bite before going out in the area. Try the Oriental Chicken!

voyage.name: Lühmanns Teestube
voyage.content: Friendly local café. Light fare and local specialties, wonderful pies, and baked goods. Their Cornish tea with fresh scones is worth trying.

voyage.name: Feldstern
voyage.content: Cozy pub/restaurant with affordable German food and outside seating in the summer. Nice lunch menu from 12:00-16:00 on weekdays.

voyage.name: Ristorante Borsalino
voyage.content: Sternstraße 125, three minutes from S-Bahn station Sternschanze in the trendy neighbourhood of Schanzenviertel. Pizzas start from €6, fresh pasta is around €7-10 (try Pasta Mista), the meat dishes are delicious (it is right next to the "Schlachthof"-Slaughterhouse) and the four course menu is at €19.50. From 12:00-15:00 they serve a lunch menu for €6.50. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Kombüse
voyage.content: Mexican meets Hamburg punk/alternative. Excellent fresh ingredients. Vegan & veggie options (but also meat for the carnivores), with a huge range of hot sauces. Prices are low (€10.50 or less as of April 2015) and portions are huge.

voyage.name: Lokmam
voyage.content: It is not without reason that a lot of Turkish people love this place. Take the S11/S31 subway and get out at Sternschanze. From there Lokmam is seven minutes away.

voyage.name: Pamukkale Grill and Restaurant
voyage.content: One of the oldest Doener stores in Hamburg. Operates a takeaway bistro and a restaurant.

voyage.name: Azeitona
voyage.content: There you can also get other great oriental food and smoke a shisha.

voyage.name: Bullerei
voyage.content: Modern and cool steak restaurant.

voyage.name: Delta Bistro
voyage.content: Surprisingly cozy atmosphere. High quality meat and fish, but the menu offers some vegetarian dishes, too. Dishes are huge and the preparation quality comes close to star-awarded locations. It is advisable to reserve a table in advance, especially on Fridays and Saturdays in the autumn and winter months.

voyage.name: Fischereihafen-Restaurant
voyage.content: Große Elbstraße 143. Excellent view of parts of the port and the river Elbe. Many celebs have dined here, including English royals.

voyage.name: The Academy
voyage.content: People in wheelchairs not always welcome.

voyage.name: Thomas Read
voyage.content: Irish pub.

voyage.name: Molotow/Top Ten Bar
voyage.content: Concert location and club.

voyage.name: Knust
voyage.content: Concert location and club

voyage.name: Headcrash
voyage.content: Concert location and club.

voyage.name: Baalsaal
voyage.content: St. Pauli, ext to the Spielbudenplatz. Usually house and electro, sometimes drum'n'bass.

voyage.name: Uebel und Gefährlich
voyage.content: In a former bunker from World War II, it can be found near St. Pauli in Feldstraße. Easy to reach with the metro U3. Music used to be more hard house and electro but is changing nowadays from day to day.

voyage.name: Tunnel
voyage.content: If you are more into Trance, Techno and Schranz the Tunnel might be a good place.

voyage.name: Cafe Klatsch
voyage.content: A small cafe serving breakfast and other tidbits in a very cozy environment with friendly staff.

voyage.name: MarYSol
voyage.content: A tapas bar.

voyage.name: Piazza
voyage.content: You will find a lot of bars and cafés here, many of Portuguese or Spanish background.

voyage.name: Christiansen's Fine Drinks & Cocktails
voyage.content: Award-winning bar (Playboy Bar of the Year 1998, Best Bartender 2000, Marcellinos Top 10, etc.), open M-Sa at 20:00.

voyage.name: BPSchanzen1
voyage.content: A tiny bar that houses many different DJs. The atmosphere is very friendly and good music is played. It's opposite the house that is occupied by various leftist fractions. (The yellow building with all the graffiti, named 'rote Flora'.)

voyage.name: Gun Club
voyage.content: Grungy but friendly punk bar in a cellar just off the Davidstraße. Came second in Hamburg Mexikanercontest (Mexikaner is a shot drink very similar to a bloody mary), and it shows - definitely the recommended drink here.

voyage.name: Komet
voyage.content: 1950s, 60s and 70s rock, soul, R&B and similar in an entirely appropriate setting with cinema couches, pulp film posters and a (rather decrepit) Wurlitzer.

voyage.name: Eldorado
voyage.content: 1960s and 1970s music in entirely period setting, with wallpaper and ceiling that seem to be completely original and at least 40 years old, and furniture to match.

voyage.name: Shebeen
voyage.content: Cheap & cheerful bar with minimalist decoration celebrating St.Pauli FC and other friendly clubs. It's a hangout of the St.Pauli Ultras. Outsiders very welcome, but if you don't agree with what St.Pauli stands for, this is not the place to be. After matches it can get a bit rough if the competition decides to come visit.

voyage.name: Washington-Bar
voyage.content: Relaxed bar covered in Hunter S. Thompson quotes with atmosphere to match. Small dance floor with DJ who plays everything from psychedelic jazz to German hip-hop. Excellent selection of gin&tonics.

voyage.name: Zur Ritze
voyage.content: Zur Ritze is fairly easy to find. It's near the Beatlesplatz at Reeperbahn; follow the signage down a small alley to the almost legendary door. The bar is almost always open, and it's a beautiful place to sit and talk all night. Having a nice night here won't break the bank, and it's a place to meet people who have made the Kiez the place it is today. The walls are full of photos, and in the basement there's a boxing

voyage.name: Pampa
voyage.content: The outdoor bars and cafes of Karolinenviertel merge with those of the southern part of the Schanzenviertel neighbourhood making one of Europe's great outdoor dining areas (at least in Summer). Pampa Bar is a great example. Plenty of relaxed lounging under the trees. Friendly table service so you don't even have to stumble to the bar to order your next drink and a good range of tasty bar meals.

voyage.name: kir
voyage.content: Gay party called "Love Pop" on Wednesdays and every 2nd Friday in the month from 23:00.

voyage.name: Strandperle
voyage.content: Considered the only "true" beach club right at the Elbe river bank with undisturbed views of the passing ships.

voyage.name: Karo Beach
voyage.content: Beachclub in Karo-Viertel. Big sand beach but no water, also family friendly.

voyage.name: Strand Pauli
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: Mon-Fri from 11:00, Sat Sun from 10:00; Nov-Mar: Mon-Fri from 17:00, Sat Sun from 10:00
voyage.content: Beachclub on different floors right at Elbe, hence great views of the river from almost all places.

voyage.name: Hamburg del Mar
voyage.content: Beach club right at the Elbe bank, next to Dock 3. View to Elbe just from the front row.

voyage.name: Dock 3
voyage.content: Beach club right at the Elbe bank, next to Hamburg del Mar. View to Elbe just from the front row.

voyage.name: Schanzenstern
voyage.content: In the middle of the trendy quarter of Schanzenviertel, 50 beds.

voyage.name: Instant Sleep Backpacker Hostel
voyage.content: 45 beds, provides a kitchen. Also in Schanzenviertel.

voyage.name: Kiezbude
voyage.content: Peter, the owner has done a tremendous job of turning an old brothel into a very unique hostel. The rooms might remind you of their former purpose but are very clean and convenient.

voyage.name: Schanzenstern Altona
voyage.content: 70 beds.

voyage.name: Superbude St. Pauli
voyage.content: Cool area with lots of hip shops, bars and near the football stadium. Large and clean, safe neighborhood.

voyage.name: Meininger Hotel
voyage.content: Double rooms start at €45 per person, dormitory starts at €18. Breakfast €5.90. Distances: 0.5 km Bahnhof Altona.

voyage.name: Elbe Camp
voyage.content: One of few options in Hamburg for campers. Beautifully located right at the Elbe river. Great for ship spotters.

voyage.name: NH Hamburg City
voyage.content: 119 suites available in a modern style.

voyage.name: Stadthaushotel
voyage.content: 13 rooms.

voyage.name: East Hotel
voyage.content: Designer hotel with one of the best lounges/bars in town. Very trendy and stylish.

voyage.name: Empire Riverside Hotel
voyage.content: A hotel in St. Pauli designed by David Chipperfield near Reeperbahn and the harbour. Each room is designed with a floor-length panoramic window that allow for a great view from any point in the room.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu
voyage.content: 4-star hotel next to the Botanical Gardens by Dammtor station, the upper floors have stunning views of the city and gardens. Connected to Conference Center Hamburg (CCH) and through it to the fairgrounds. Prices skyrocket during trade fairs.

voyage.name: Hamburg Stadtpark
voyage.content: 150 ha of park with a pretty good Planetarium at an old water tower in its middle, multiple sporting areas and boat rental on the lake.

voyage.name: Alsterpark
voyage.content: Inaugurated in 1952. The part west of the Alster is called Alstervorland, the one east Alterpark.

voyage.name: Eimsbüttler Park
voyage.content: This former forest and current park has survived both world wars and still offers green pastures around the Weiher lake together with a playground, swimming pool and a café.

voyage.name: Tierpark Hagenbeck
voyage.price: Adults: €20, children 4–16 years: €15, family: €60-70, with Tropen-Aquarium: €30, children: 21 EUR, family: €85-98
voyage.content: Hamburg's Zoo. The collection began in 1863 with animals that belonged to Carl Hagenbeck Sr. (1810–1887), a fishmonger who became an amateur animal collector. The park itself was founded by Carl Hagenbeck Jr. in 1907. It is known for being the first zoo to use open enclosures surrounded by moats, rather than barred cages, to better approximate animals' natural environments.

voyage.name: Friedhof Ohlsdorf
voyage.content: One of the world's biggest graveyards.

voyage.name: Imam-Ali-Mosque
voyage.content: Biggest of all mosques in Hamburg. Centre of the religious and cultural life of the huge Iranian community. The Imams of Hamburg happen to have played important roles in Iran's religious and political everyday life since their installation in the 1950s.

voyage.name: Museum am Rothenbaum - Kulturen und Kunste der Welt
voyage.content: Formerly known as the Museum of Ethnology. The museum has ethnographic objects from around the world.

voyage.name: Alster Cruise
voyage.content: The obvious thing to do is to take a ride around the Alster on one of the leisure boats and enjoy the greenery and elegant buildings around it.

voyage.name: Ernst-Deutsch-Theater
voyage.content: The Ernst-Deutsch-Theater has been an established part of the Hamburg theatre scene since 1951. Today, it is the largest privately operated playhouse in Germany.

voyage.name: The English Theatre of Hamburg
voyage.content: The English Theatre of Hamburg performs from September through June, giving eight performances per week.

voyage.name: The Hamburg Players
voyage.content: Hamburg's oldest English-language theatre group giving three shows a year at the Theater in der Marschnerstraße.

voyage.name: Supper Club
voyage.content: Supper Club's name doesn't give you any clues about this business. It hires canoes and all manner of other unpowered water craft by the hour. When you have finished paddling you can eat at the outdoor cafe if you wish. A 2 hour paddle using one of their suggested itineraries through small canals and lakes takes you past some of Hamburg's most elegant homes, You will definitely want to move there after this paddle (wh

voyage.name: Hamburg Planetarium
voyage.content: Features multiple visual shows a day, and an observation deck.

voyage.name: Bäderland Holthusenbad
voyage.content: Swimming pool. Basic entry gives access to pools and thermen (warm and cold water pools). Sauna complex for an additional fee.

voyage.name: Isemarkt
voyage.content: Europe's longest open market, under the U3 subway driveway between Hoheluftbrücke and Eppendorfer Baum between the two lanes of the Isestraße.

voyage.name: Der Etrusker
voyage.content: Small and quite crowded Italian restaurant in the "Grindel" district near the university. Excellent Italian classics (pizza, pasta, etc.) for reasonable money. A lot of Italian restaurants as alternative to the left and right if you don't get a table. For dinner: make sure you are early (before 7pm) or make a reservation (only by phone).

voyage.name: La Monella
voyage.content: Hamburg's first vegetarian Italian restaurant. Small menu with Italian standards. Daily menu with dishes made of regional ingredients. Good place for a very delicious vegetarian lunch on a budget. Dinner slightly overpriced.

voyage.name: Alster Cliff
voyage.content: Nice place to stop for coffee and cake or a meal with a good view on the Alster lake. Lunch food (salad, pizza, pasta) are of average quality and above average price.

voyage.name: Restaurant Kalliopea
voyage.content: Traditional Greek food.

voyage.name: ZaZa-Bar
voyage.content: Small bar in a trendy neighbourhood that serves good drinks and has an interesting crowd of customers: some shoppers that celebrate their latest fashions, office workers that cool down, night owls that warm up, and quite few people who live in the area and just drop in for a drink. Has chairs outside. Happy Hour from 5PM-9PM and all night on Mondays.

voyage.name: Logo
voyage.content: Concert location.

voyage.name: Down Under
voyage.content: Australian-themed bar with lots of cocktails (€5-10), burgers (chicken burger €6, beef burger €8, ostrich burger €9.50), chicken wings (also all you can eat on Tuesdays).

voyage.name: Camping Buchholz
voyage.content: All year round.

voyage.name: Knaus Campingpark
voyage.content: From April to October.

voyage.name: Courtyard Hamburg Airport
voyage.content: The traditional country manor-style Courtyard close to the airport.

voyage.name: Lindner Park Hotel Hagenbeck
voyage.content: A 4-star hotel less than 3 km from the Hamburger Sportveiren. A comfortable hotel, convenient for football fans, featuring a fitness room and sauna.

voyage.name: Dorint Hotel Hamburg Eppendorf
voyage.content: The hotel offers 195 rooms including 14 suites and has direct connection to the adjoining university hospital.

voyage.name: Grand Elysee
voyage.content: Despite not being affiliated with any of the American hotel chains, Hamburg's largest hotel of over 500 rooms tries to emulate the 1990s American idea of a luxury hotel. The hotel serves a large on-site conference centre and features extensive spa and wellness facilities.

voyage.name: The Fontenay
voyage.content: Upscale hotel opened in 2018.

voyage.name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe
voyage.price: Adult €10, reduced €7, children under 18 years free, family €17
voyage.address: Steintorplatz, just to the southeast of Hauptbahnhof
voyage.content: The museum is a leading centre for art, applied art, and design. Its collections of work from Europe and the Middle and the Far East are of the finest-quality and span all epochs from the Ancient World to the present day. They also have many activities and concerts (see the Classical Music section). The museum is housed in an 18th-century palace, which has the original roofs and ceilings.

voyage.name: Dreieinigkeitskirche St. Georg
voyage.content: Baroque church in Sankt Georg.

voyage.name: St.-Marien-Dom St. Georg
voyage.content: Since 1995, this neo-romanesque church is the cathedral of the youngest Roman Catholic archbishop of Germany. Though the church has not the splendor one might expect, next to it you may find the first statue world wide of the late pope, John-Paul II.

voyage.name: Bergedorf Castle
voyage.content: This is the only preserved castle inside the city borders of Hamburg, and it has been mentioned in documents in the 14th century. Since 1953 it houses a museum of Bergedorf and the Vierlande region. The idyllic castle park has been protected since 1926.

voyage.name: Bergedorf City Hall
voyage.content: This castle-like villa was built in 1898-99 and has hosted the city government of Bergedorf since 1927. It is also open to visitors, as is the 35 m high city hall tower (Rathausturm). There is a park (Rathauspark) behind the city hall with a scene, playground, stream and garden artworks.

voyage.name: Hamburger Sternwarte
voyage.content: The astrophysics faculty of the Universität Hamburg is spread over a big park with protected neobaroque buildings with historical equipment for astronomy science including different telescopes. There's a visitor center with a café and tours every Sunday or by appointment.

voyage.name: Petri und Pauli Kirche
voyage.content: A Lutheran church, and together with the castle the most important historical building in Bergedorf. The first church was built here in 1162, the current one was opened in 1502.

voyage.name: Kirche St. Michael
voyage.content: Built in 1955 in the form of a white cube extended in the east by the altar room, in the north by the sacristy and in the west by the lobby. The church is in the middle of the old graveyard.

voyage.name: Franz-von-Assisi-Kirche
voyage.content: One of the newest churches in the region, this Lutheran church was inaugurated in 1993. The 40-m-high church tower is visible from far away.

voyage.name: Edith-Stein-Kirche
voyage.content: A modern Catholic church building inaugurated in 1993. It is a round church with a flat roof rising up towards the altar.

voyage.name: Rieck Haus - Vierländer Freilichtmuseum
voyage.content: Open-air museum showcasing the rural life in the Vierlanden before the industrial revolution. The premises was an active farm operated by the Rieck family up until WWII. There are still farm animals there, and several hands-on experiences for visitors such as milking cows.

voyage.name: Riepenburger Mühle
voyage.hours: open in Apr-Oct, Tue and Thu 14:00-18:00 and the 1st and 3rd Sun each month 13:00-17:00
voyage.content: Windmill built in 1828, though the first windmill at this place was already built in 1318. It has a shop and café, and in the nearby former warehouse there's an interesting shop with local art.

voyage.name: Hof Eggers
voyage.hours: open in Mar-Dec: Fri Sat 12:00-18,:00 Sun 10:00-18:00
voyage.content: Farm open to visitors with a café, shop, and four cottages.

voyage.name: Reitbrooker Mühle
voyage.content: Built in 1870, this windmill is next to the Reitbrooker Mühlenbrücke ("mill bridge"). This is a so-called "Galerieholländer" windmill; a square two-story stone building with a wooden octagon building on the top. It was used until as a windmill 1938 or 1939, and became a protected building in 1942. It still functions as a mill, albeit not a wind powered one. When the fodder shop is open, you can also see the mill from

voyage.name: Kirche St. Severini
voyage.content: The biggest church in the Vierlande region. First built as a stone church in 1319, and thoroughly renovated in the late 18th century.

voyage.name: Kirche St. Johannis
voyage.content: After an earlier church, presumably made of rocks, was destroyed by flooding, this timber-framed one was built in 1599-1603. It is an open church and as such can generally be visited anytime (during daytime).

voyage.name: Kirche St. Nicolai
voyage.content: First mentioned in documents from 1247, this is the oldest of the village churches in the Vierlande.

voyage.name: Kirche St. Johannis
voyage.content: The oldest major church in Hamburg, mentioned in documents from 1261. It has been remodeled and expanded several times, though part of the walls are still from the 13th century. The wooden 26.2-m-high church tower was constructed in 1630.

voyage.name: St. Pankratius
voyage.content: This 17th-century church features carvings depicting scenes from the Old and New Testaments, and an organ by the famous organ builder Arp Schnitger.

voyage.name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe
voyage.content: The Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe Hamburg has many smaller concerts — something almost every day — and is much cheaper than the Laeiszhalle. The programs range from the curator of their early keyboard instrument collection playing them and giving a spiel on the music and the instruments (in German only!) to formal concerts of renditions of Schubert's Die Winterreise. Pick up a schedule at the desk of the museum (down

voyage.name: Deutsches Schauspielhaus
voyage.content: The biggest German speech theatre looks back on a famous tradition. Gustav Gründgens, Ivan Nagel, and Peter Zadek staged highlights in German theatre history here.

voyage.name: Geelhaus
voyage.content: Menu changes frequently, fresh food, creativity.

voyage.name: McBoat
voyage.hours: Open 24 hours but closed in winter
voyage.content: The only McDonald's that you can order your meal (on its app) and have it delivered to the shores while paddling along the canal. The meal is prepared fresh in the restaurant right next to the shoreline.

voyage.name: Al Lido
voyage.content: Excellent Italian and Pizzeria

voyage.name: Restaurant Cox
voyage.price: Dinner including wine is approximately €30-40. They have a value lunch deal (two course menu for €11)
voyage.content: Trendy restaurant with consistently good international cuisine, often local German dishes

voyage.name: Vasco da Gama
voyage.content: Good Portuguese and German food.

voyage.name: Bergedorfer Schlosscafé
voyage.content: Castle café on the inner yard of Bergedorf Castle.

voyage.name: Block Haus
voyage.content: Steak restaurant in a timber-framed house where there have been hospitality businesses for several decades.

voyage.name: Café Chrysander
voyage.content: Cafe and restaurant at the edge of Bergedorf Castle Park with lunch, breakfast buffet, home made cakes and a range of special coffees. In the evening the place becomes a cultural club with regular concerts, movie presentations and lectures.

voyage.name: Zollenspieker Fährhaus
voyage.content: Big restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating and a bar. They have many different menus to choose from; mainly Mediterranean and Northern German cuisine. The complex also includes a hotel and a spa.

voyage.name: Cafe Gnosa
voyage.content: Coffeehouse with wide range of delicious self-made cakes and pastries. Famous for its cake buffet, also a great place to have breakfast or lunch. Gay-owned. Customers mixed by straight and gay people of any age. May not be easy to catch a table during rush-hours. For sugar- and caffeine-addicts.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Hamburg
voyage.content: Outdated, worn and quite out of the way, with limited transit options. Pluses include breakfast and proximity to Elbpark for a walk or jog in the morning. Free soft drinks in minibar.

voyage.name: Ibis Hamburg Alster Centrum
voyage.content: This is just like any other hotel in the Ibis chain — clean basic rooms with bathroom, TV and Wi-Fi. They have a bar and a restaurant too.

voyage.name: Suite Novotel Hamburg City
voyage.content: A large midscale hotel aimed at travellers staying for longer periods. Rooms have a small kitchenette and many come with extra sofa-beds. Unfortunately, the old Suite Novotel standards are far behind what more modern hotels offer. That said, the hotel is in a tall tower, so if you manage to get a room in one of the upper floors, you can enjoy a nice view of Hamburg.

voyage.name: Mercure Hamburg City
voyage.content: The hotel's slightly offside location makes it accessible by car and quite cosy. The neighbourhood consists of late 20th century development over canals, which may not be the most interesting in Hamburg, but the Hammerbrook S-Bahn station is a short walk away. The hotel's highlight is the floating event space Kai 10, unfortunately as of 2015 only available for special events. The hotel is easily accessibly by car.

voyage.name: Le Royal Meridien
voyage.content: One of the best hotels overlooking the Alster lake. Each room is designed in the "Art & Tech" design. Restaurant with nice view over the lake and spa.

voyage.name: Hotel Atlantic Kempinski
voyage.content: The grande dame of Hamburg has grown to be an internationally recognized paragon of luxury hospitality.

voyage.name: Reichshof Hamburg, Curio Collection by Hilton
voyage.content: 4-star hotel that provides various dining options, gym, business centre, parking and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Container port
voyage.content: Hamburg's massive container ports line the southern bank of the river Elbe. They are most spectacular at night, and the best place to view them from is by driving north along the A7 highway (heading into the Elbtunnel tunnel). They are not freely accessible to the public, but there are bus tours (only in German, about €35 per person, must be booked in advance) which depart from Hamburg's city centre and, over the cou

voyage.name: Aussichtspunkt Steinwerder
voyage.content: A viewing platform at the southern end of the Alter Elbtunnel, with great views on Landungsbrücken, the Elbphilharmonie, and Hamburg's harbourfront.

voyage.name: Pfarrkirche St. Pankratius in Neuenfelde
voyage.content: 17th century church, famous for the biggest organ Arp Schnitger built.

voyage.name: BallinStadt Auswanderwelt Hamburg
voyage.content: It was built in 1892 under the guidance of Albert Ballin to provide medical care and accommodation to migrants, who were emigrating to the United States on HAPAG ships. The complex was converted into a museum, though its original design and layout is not the same because parts of the complex were destroyed. The museum is dedicated to the 5 million people who emigrated via Hamburg. It has a computer terminal where vis

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum Hamburg
voyage.content: Museum presenting prehistorical and early historical northern Germany as well as the history of the city of Harburg.

voyage.name: Sammlung Falckenberg
voyage.content: The Falckenberg Collection of the Cultural Foundation Phönix Art is a notable collection of modern art. Public tours Saturday on afternoons, you can also visit other times by calling ahead.

voyage.name: Freilichtmuseum am Kiekeberg
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, closed Christmas and New Year
voyage.content: Open air museum showcasing rural life with a historical alcohol distillery, teaching kitchen, museum shop.

voyage.name: Wildpark Schwarze Berge
voyage.content: This spacious wildlife zoo can be a more relaxed alternative to Hagenbeck's Tierpark and is a favourite for families. It showcases mainly local fauna in large enclosures, set in a beautiful landscape.

voyage.name: Theater im Hafen Hamburg
voyage.content: Watch The Lion King here. For many Germans this is the must-do when visiting Hamburg.

voyage.name: Stage Theater an der Elbe
voyage.content: Another musical venue. Mary Poppins is showing here until Aug 2019, then Pretty Woman will take the stage in Sep 2019.

voyage.name: CinemaxX Hamburg-Harburg
voyage.content: Cinema.

voyage.name: Harburger Berge
voyage.content: At the city (state) border and continue in to Lower Saxony, the part in Hamburg is classified as a natural park. Viewpoints offer good views over the Elbe valley all the way to Altona. One of them is at Opferberg, where according to a legend a treasure is hidden.

voyage.name: Fischbeker Heide
voyage.content: Nature reserve.

voyage.name: Atmos
voyage.content: Wellness with bio sauna (75°C), Finnish sauna (90°C) and outdoor sauna, indoor and outdoor pool, hot tub, etc. Drinks except alcohol are included in the entrance fee. In line with the German sauna culture, facilities are to be used naked for hygiene reasons, and swimwear is not allowed. Towels, bathrobes, and slippers are provided and included in the entrance fee. With a focus on relaxation and quietness, children ar

voyage.name: Rollercoaster Restaurant
voyage.content: This "Rollercoaster-Restaurant" is somewhat of a gimmicky place. Your food arrives through a "rollercoaster" in a closed pot. Some of it even does a loop in front of you. Portion size is on the small side and prices are normal.

voyage.name: La Patina
voyage.content: Good Italian style pizza, many vegetarian and vegan options.

voyage.name: Aomame
voyage.content: Asian fusion-kitchen, tapas and bowls, many vegan options, decent prices, good food.

voyage.name: Hotel Jeta
voyage.content: A modern hotel on a 3-minute walk from the . Rooms aren't particularly fancy, but the hotel will serve business travellers well.

voyage.name: Kleines Hotel Heimfeld, Harburg
voyage.content: This hotel has a station Eißendorfer Pferdeweg on bus line 44 connecting to Harburg station or you may walk to there. The hotel is small (the name correctly describes), the rooms at House 2 are even smaller, but the price is low comparing to other hotels in Hamburg.
